categories.name: build
why: P2 because it is a durable, user-facing portability improvement to the official release binaries rather than a fix for existing breakage
It unblocks running bitcoind on old glibc distros, non-glibc systems (musl, NixOS), containers, and embedded devices, with real deployment demand cited (nodl hardware on Ubuntu 18)
Extensive multi-month community testing across architectures corroborates the practical value, though it is not fixing an active regression or release-blocking defect

result.summary: This PR changes the Guix release build for Linux to produce a `-static-pie` bitcoind (and CLI utilities) using a custom GCC 14/glibc 2.44 toolchain, instead of dynamically linking against the host's glibc. It adds a new toolchains.scm module, patches glibc to disable NSS dlopen and strip nondeterministic store paths, adjusts the security/symbol checkers to validate static ELF binaries, and documents the resulting change in DNS/NSS resolution behavior in a release note. bitcoin-qt remains dynamically linked; only bitcoind and CLI tools become static-pie for x86_64 and aarch64 so far.
result.problem: Guix release binaries currently depend on the host's glibc version and dynamic linker, which breaks on very old distros, non-glibc systems (Alpine, NixOS), minimal containers, and unusual environments, and ties supported OS versions to an aging pinned glibc. Users needing to run official binaries on old or nonstandard Linux systems (e.g. embedded hardware still on Ubuntu 18.04) currently cannot easily do so.

open_concerns: Whether the removed dlopen-based NSS lookup (mDNS/.local, LDAP, SSSD, etc.) could silently break name resolution for niche setups; addressed via a release note but the underlying behavior change stands as an accepted tradeoff (willcl-ark, sedited, xrviv, 151henry151).

hebasto's concern that the FORTIFY_SOURCE symbol check no longer distinguishes libc's own fortified symbols from Bitcoin Core's; author acknowledged the check is losing significance but has not devised a fully robust replacement.
Minor open question from hebasto about whether four modules in linux_static.scm are actually needed (unresolved at last check, low materiality).
resolved_concerns: Early confusion about builds appearing dynamically linked (Frank-GER) traced to using an older/incorrect commit, resolved once rebuilt on the correct commit.
CMake linker-flag / -Werror=dev discussion resolved by author explaining tradeoffs.
hebasto's inline nits and commit-ordering suggestions addressed in subsequent pushes.

Extensive concern threads about NSS/DNS resolution correctness resolved via testing (dergoegge, 0xB10C, xrviv, theStack) showing DNS seeding, signet sync, and getnetworkinfo work correctly across many distros.

categories.rationale: Substantially improves portability of official release binaries: 'They can now be run on non-glibc based systems, as well as on systems that ship with older glibcs' (release note). It also removes a class of host-library-mismatch bugs and reduces dependence on a deliberately old pinned glibc, but it is a new capability rather than a fix for an active regression or release blocker, and carries an accepted NSS-resolution tradeoff, keeping it at P2 rather than P1.

result.card: This long-running Guix build PR (opened 2022, still active in 2026) makes the Linux release bitcoind and CLI tools fully static and position-independent (`-static-pie`) using a custom GCC 14/glibc 2.44 toolchain, so binaries no longer depend on the host's glibc/dynamic linker. The problem it solves: official release binaries currently fail or behave inconsistently on very old, unusual, or non-glibc Linux systems (Alpine, NixOS, minimal containers, old distros), a pain point corroborated by a user citing embedded hardware stuck on Ubuntu 18.04 ('We need them for nodl as older devices are based on Ubuntu 18 and won't be upgraded'). The change has been extensively validated by dozens of independent builders and testers across architectures and distros over months, with multiple approach/concept ACKs (dergoegge, w0xlt, willcl-ark, hebasto, jsarenik) and no unresolved blocking objections, though a real tradeoff (loss of dynamic NSS module resolution for things like mDNS/.local) is accepted and documented rather than fixed. The PR is currently rebased on top of the still-open #36272/#36193 guix toolchain-split PRs, so reviewers should start there; within this PR itself nothing is known to be blocking review. It also closes long-standing issue #19075 on aarch64 pointer authentication.
